Adoption of draft report on CO2 standards
                                                
                                                
                                                
                                                
                                                    12-11-2026 - 16:03
                                                
                                                
                                                
                                            
On 4 November 2026, the ENVI committee voted on the draft report regarding CO2 standards. Regulation (EU) 2019/631 setting CO₂ emission performance standards for new passenger cars and light commercial vehicles constitutes a central element of the Union’s Fit for 55 framework and broader objective of achieving climate neutrality by 2050 under the European Climate Law.
Through the proposal, the Commission seeks to adapt the existing framework to evolving market and technological conditions by introducing additional compliance flexibilities for manufacturers while maintaining the overall contribution of the transport sector to the Union’s climate objectives.
The proposal notably revises the 2030 fleet-wide CO₂ reduction target for vans from 50% to 40%, compared with the 2021 baseline, reduces the 2035 fleet-wide target from 100% to 90% for both cars and vans, and introduces the possibility to compensate the remaining emissions through fuel credits and low-carbon steel credits. The proposal also introduces a harmonized EU framework for vehicle labelling and consumer information, including new obligations for manufacturers and distributors as regards vehicle labels and a product database. A total of 1036 amendments were tabled. A comprehensive compromise amendment was negotiated, covering all amendments tabled. The compromise amendment notably sets the 2035 CO₂ reduction targets at 87.5% for cars and 80% for vans, and the 2030 target for vans at 35%. It also introduces additional flexibilities for manufacturers, including multi-year averaging of emissions, super-credits for certain electric vehicles made in the EU, and credits for the use of low-carbon steel produced in the EU. Furthermore, it provides for the recognition of vehicles running exclusively on eligible fuels as zero-emission vehicles from 2030.
